A week after a midterms
"[bloodbath](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-was-way)"
throttled the GOP and [humiliated](https://zeteo.com/p/sex-crimes-lies-war-
money-magas-2026) the president, the Trump administration has been plunged
into another intense round of chaotic backbiting, bitter infighting at the
highest levels of the U.S. government, and international scandal that even has
Republican lawmakers demanding answers and accountability.

In the wake of the 2026 electoral "blue tsunami," the Trumpland elite [had
already begun eating itself alive](https://zeteo.com/p/maga-self-immolated-
how-everything), in an escalating series of blame games, turf battles, and
highly personal, petty blood feuds. Now, MAGAworld is self-cannibalizing over
_yet another_ colossal, shambolic mess of their own making.

In recent days, the Nvidia sex scandal and alleged spying and chip-smuggling
debacle have created a blast radius that reaches far within Donald Trump's
administration. It has drawn further scrutiny to the president's hyper-cozy
relationship with Nvidia's now-ousted CEO Jensen Huang, and raised additional
questions about why Trump didn't respond forcefully after he'd been given
multiple intelligence warnings about Huang's relationship with a suspected
Chinese spy. President Trump's downplaying of these warnings, including from
his own Secretary of State Marco Rubio earlier this year, has been reported on
by major [news outlets](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/10/us/politics/trump-
china-trip-nvidia.html); **Zeteo** can confirm, per sources familiar with the
situation, that the president knew and, in the words of one person involved in
the matter, "didn't take it seriously enough." Huang, a towering figure in the
AI industry, continued to advise Trump on policies directly affecting his
business and trade.

The rapidly expanding scandal has also ballooned to the point that it ignited
a new civil war at the most senior ranks of the Trump-Vance administration,
with several of the president's cabinet members and top advisers spitefully
trying to engineer the firing of one of their own: the cabinet secretary who
has made _so many_ enemies within the past two years of the second Trump era
that his own colleagues frequently call him things like "[that fucking
dumbass.](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-jeffrey-epstein-howard-lutnick-blackmail)"
